analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (838–1644) and the bounded change excerpt at HEAD 3541–3575. The complete range map places changes outside these BASE excerpts; their existing cache, media, cancellation, resource-retirement, billing and encrypted-stream descriptions are not PR regressions. Relevant contracts include T-041 account-scoped encrypted checkpoint reuse, T-008 fail-closed response encryption, T-010 cancellation, T-027 weight identity, T-050 media plaintext handling and T-053 connection-bound authorization. The existing reconnect/session limitation at BASE 1551–1559 must not be reported as newly introduced.
The added documentation describes setup/control listeners restarting after cable-address or pairing changes, stopping when pairing is absent, and retaining their state when the pairing store is unreadable. Pairing identity excludes the edge secret and relies on a fresh link epoch per ceremony. No supplied evidence establishes an exploitable new behavior or an invalidated mitigation: this is a documentation change, and its listener implementation and preceding distributed-cluster contract are outside these units.
Integration should inspect the supplied changes, if any, to provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Inference/Distributed/Onboarding/ClusterService.swift, especially listenerChange, ensureResponder and ensureControl, and ClusterSetupLinkExchange.Pairing.Identity/Responder. Verify fresh epochs, handshake authentication, actual listener closure and control-lease invalidation across rotation/removal, and whether unreadable stores retain revoked pairing authority. This distributed trust boundary is not detailed in the supplied canonical definitions; reconcile it with the rest of the PR before deciding whether the threat model needs expansion. The truncated patch and missing implementation limit that conclusion, rather than proving a vulnerability or safety.
